comparison: Perfect claim overlap (C66-C68) on alternative evolutionary hypotheses. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting the homologous endothermy hypothesis contradicts isotope data and seasonal endothermy is untestable. Peer reviewer explicitly rejects the plausibility, stating reversals to ectothermy are implausible and the argument is 'much less sound.' Both express skepticism but peer review is more dismissive.

Perfect claim overlap (C5, C69-C73) on climate-endothermy connections. OpenEval rates as UNSUPPORTED, noting speculative causal links without direct evidence and circular reasoning. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, finding the direction interesting but conditional on resolving uncertainties about which taxa were actually endothermic. Both question the support but peer review is slightly more open to the hypothesis.

High claim overlap (C26, C28-C35) on theoretical framework. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the isotope methodology and theoretical principles well-founded. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer #3 challenging fundamental assumptions about ectotherm body temperatures and suggesting the contrast between ectotherm and endotherm values may be overestimated by 'a factor of two or more.' Major disagreement on theoretical foundation.

High claim overlap (C78-C81) on diagenesis screening methods. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting the approach is standard practice. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer #3 directly challenging the phosphate preservation assumption, citing violations of this 'rule of thumb' and preferring microscopy/minor element mapping. Significant disagreement on methodological adequacy.

Substantial claim overlap (C49-C54) on African Kannemeyeriiformes endothermy. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on isotope data falling within predicted ranges. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, noting Reviewer #3's fundamental concerns about theoretical models and ecological assignments apply to all endothermy interpretations. Disagreement stems from different confidence in underlying assumptions.

Moderate claim overlap (C37-C40) on Permian therapsid ectothermy. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding data consistent with ectothermic interpretation. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer #3 questioning ecological assignments as 'often debated' and involving 'circular reasoning,' recommending focus on 'unambiguous cases.' Disagreement on interpretation confidence.

Moderate claim overlap (C55-C58) on synthesis and timing. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to uneven support and limited sampling. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer #2 explicitly identifying uncertainty about Lystrosaurus and criticizing misleading presentation in main text versus supplement. Both agree on uncertainty but peer review emphasizes communication issues.

Moderate claim overlap (C44-C46) on Lystrosaurus interpretation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting critical assumptions about reference taxa. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer #2 explicitly stating 'fair amount of uncertainty' and criticizing that main text makes it 'seem like Lystrosaurus is definitely an endotherm, which seems kind of misleading.' Strong agreement on uncertainty.

Moderate claim overlap (C61-C64) on cynodont phylogenetic inferences. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to limited taxonomic sampling and lack of intermediate taxa. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, noting this evolutionary conclusion depends on isotope interpretations that have been questioned and Reviewer #3 states the study doesn't 'offer a strong new constraint on the question of therapsid physiology.' Strong agreement on insufficient support.

Moderate claim overlap (C3-C4, C65) on primary conclusions about independent origins. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting reliance on uncertain interpretations and incomplete sampling. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer #2 noting uncertainty 'has important implications for your evolutionary scenarios' and Reviewer #3 questioning the overall constraint provided. Strong agreement that main conclusions are not well-supported.

Moderate claim overlap (C19-C25) on fibrolamellar bone as endothermy proxy. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate critical evaluation of limitations. Peer reviewer rates as SUPPORTED, with Reviewer #2 agreeing that FLB 'is more a reflection of the rate at which bone tissue is being formed than endothermy in a strict sense' and recommending thoughtful presentation. Strong agreement on nuanced interpretation.

Moderate claim overlap (C41-C43) on Sinophoneus interpretation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging only two specimens and ambiguous interpretation. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, with concerns about ecological assignments being 'often debated' and involving 'circular reasoning' applying to this case. Agreement on uncertainty.

Moderate claim overlap (C74-C75) on sample collection. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting clear documentation. Peer reviewer rates as SUPPORTED, with Reviewer #3 stating 'I see no reason to question the significance of the samples studied or the quality of the isotopic measurements.' Strong agreement on data quality.

Low claim overlap (C47-C48) on Chinese kannemeyeriiformes. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to circular reasoning about Shansisuchus thermophysiology. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, noting fundamental concerns about theoretical models apply to these interpretations. Agreement on uncertainty but peer review focuses on broader theoretical issues.

Low claim overlap (C12-C15) on secondary palate. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for critical evaluation of this proxy. Peer reviewer rates as SUPPORTED, providing factual corrections about dicynodont anatomy but not challenging the interpretation that presence in ectotherms questions the endothermy link. Agreement with minor technical corrections.

Low claim overlap (C16-C18) on turbinates/turbinals. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for discussion of this proxy. Peer reviewer rates as SUPPORTED, recommending additional citations (Owerkowicz et al., 2015) but not challenging the claims. Agreement with suggestions for additional references.

OpenEval evaluates introductory claims (C1, C6-C9) about modern endothermy and bird evolution as SUPPORTED based on established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval evaluates claim C2 summarizing prior anatomical evidence as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this background summary claim.
